papers.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
papers.abstract: Slow-wave sleep preserves the capacity for spontaneous or stimulus-evoked awakening despite reduced responsiveness, yet how thalamic nuclei coordinate to preserve arousability remains unclear. We analysed six fMRI and EEG datasets spanning sleep, propofol anesthesia and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS). During N2 and N3, centromedian (CM) and ventral posterolateral (VPL) nuclei showed convergent edge-community profiles and increased closed-loop intra-thalamic motifs, changes not observed during anesthesia or UWS. During N3, directed effective connectivity along CM[->]VPL[->]pulvinar (PUL) increased versus wakefulness and N2. Stronger CM[->]VPL and VPL[->]PUL connectivity covaried with greater N3 delta power, which was higher before awakening than before transitions to N2 and positively associated with three-month improvement in behavioural responsiveness in UWS. These findings identify a CM-VPL-PUL-centred pattern of intra-thalamic organization linked to preserved arousability during slow-wave sleep, extending accounts focused on individual nuclei and thalamocortical interactions.

papers.title: Multiple platform-induced sleep restriction disrupts time-of-day-dependent corticosterone and leukocyte profiles in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.abstract: Sleep restriction (SR) is recognized to alter neuroendocrine and immune parameters, yet whether these changes reflect overall alterations in signal magnitude or temporal shifts in systemic dynamics remains poorly defined. We evaluated the effects of subchronic sleep restriction on the 24-h diurnal profiles of serum corticosterone (CS), total white blood cell (WBC) counts, and granulocyte-enriched proportions in mice. Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to subchronic sleep restriction using the multiple-platform procedure or maintained under control conditions. Serum CS, total circulating WBC counts defined by FSC/SSC gating, and granulocyte-enriched percentages were measured across distinct Zeitgeber times and analyzed using two-way ANOVA with Holm corrections for multiple testing. Daily mean corticosterone levels and total WBC counts did not differ significantly between groups. A significant treatment × time interaction occurred for serum CS (p < 0.001), but time-point differences lost significance after Holm correction (p ≥ 0.06). Total WBC counts showed a borderline interaction (p = 0.050) with no time-point differences post-correction ≥, and CS-WBC correlations were not significant (p > 0.05). Conversely, granulocyte-enriched percentages exhibited a significant interaction (p = 0.002) and retained significant group differences post-correction at ZT5 (36.07 ± 2.57% vs. 18.10 ± 5.59%, adjusted p = 0.005) and ZT11 (53.03 ± 0.21% vs. 84.86 ± 8.64, adjusted p = 0.006). The multiple-platform procedure is associated with time-specific differences in serum CS and granulocyte-enriched percentages without altering the diurnal mean CS or total WBC counts. Lacking direct mechanistic measurements, these data reflect potential temporal variations under sleep restriction paradigms rather than established corticosterone-mediated regulation, clock disruption, or altered tissue homing.

papers.title: Rest promotes microglial clearance of degenerating neurons
papers.abstract: How the brain coordinates the removal of degenerating neurons with host rest and activity remains poorly understood. Using longitudinal two-photon imaging in mice with cytosolic TDP-43 proteinopathy, we show that microglia remove neuronal corpses through an ordered sequence of reaching, approaching, isolating and digesting. Clearance was higher during the light (resting) phase and lower during the dark (active) phase. This pattern reversed after light-dark cycle inversion and was blunted by sleep disruption. Chemogenetic inhibition of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons increased engulfment during the active phase, while activation and inhibition of the {beta}2-adrenergic receptor ADRB2 suppressed and enhanced clearance, respectively, identifying noradrenergic signaling as a brake on engulfment. However, sustained microglial ADRB2 deletion impaired clearance and blunted light-dark differences. These findings reveal that microglial removal of degenerating neurons is enhanced during rest and support a role for noradrenergic signaling in coordinating this cellular maintenance process with the host's rest-activity cycle.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.abstract: Infradian cycles are multi-day oscillations whose mechanisms are still poorly understood, while circadian rhythms have been extensively studied and are well-documented in mammals. In this study, we monitored the locomotor activity of three rodent species: CD-1 mice (Mus musculus), Mongolian gerbils (Meriones unguiculatus), and white-tailed antelope squirrels (Ammospermophilus leucurus). We used Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to verify the prevalence of circadian and infradian rhythms, the magnitude of the spectral power, and associations across species, rhythms, and sexes. Circadian rhythms were robust and were found for all animals. For infradian rhythms, the prevalence in mice was extremely low, whereas the prevalence in gerbils and squirrels was moderate in the 5- and 10-day ranges. In all cases, the strength of infradian rhythmicity was less than 10% of the strength of circadian rhythmicity. As no natural environmental cycle is documented to operate in the 5- to 10-day range, further studies are needed to determine whether an endogenous source may account for this weak but significant infradian rhythmicity.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is important for diagnosing and managing sleep disorders. However, artificial intelligence-based models still struggle with explainability, sequence plausibility, and personalization across subjects. We propose LogicSleep, a neurosymbolic framework that integrates transition rules with deep learning models for explainable, physiologically valid, and subject-adaptive sleep staging. LogicSleep extracts multi-level evidence from raw polysomnography via a CNN-graph U-Net backbone, providing explainable patterns beyond classification. Sequence plausibility is enforced by combining Conditional Random Fields with Deep Learning with Differentiable Logics (DL2) rules, which discourage implausible transitions, promote physiologically valid ones, and regularize dwell times; the same rules also guide subject-specific test-time adaptation via entropy minimization. Across different datasets (i.e., ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3 datasets), under both within- and cross-dataset settings, LogicSleep consistently outperforms strong baselines and improves sequence-level metrics. Ablations confirm complementary contributions of each component. LogicSleep advances sleep staging toward physiologically plausible, personalized, and explainable predictions.

papers.title: Effects of pharmacotherapy on quantitative electroencephalogram measures of sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Recent studies of noradrenergic and antimuscarinic agents to treat obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) have been promising, but their impact on subjective and objective sleep quality and daytime sleepiness have shown inconsistent results. This study aimed to assess the effects of the noradrenergic agent reboxetine alone and in combination with the antimuscarinic oxybutynin on next-day objective sleepiness through quantitative analysis of wake electroencephalography (qEEG) during a Karolinska Drowsiness Test (KDT). This was a secondary analysis from a randomised trial of reboxetine alone and in combination with oxybutynin versus placebo in 16 participants with OSA. All participates have undergone a KDT in the evening prior to drug or placebo administration and sleep opportunity, and ∼1hr post-waking next morning. Mixed models were used to examine drug effects on qEEG outcomes. There was no significant main effect of treatment (Reboxetine vs placebo vs Reboxetine-Oxybutynin) on slow EEG frequencies or theta/alpha ratio during the morning KDT. There was a significant main effect of testing time (evening vs morning) with higher morning delta and theta EEG power during eyes open and the delta power during entire KDT (all p < 0.001) compared to the evening test. There was a significant main effect of electrode position (F3, C3, O1), on wake delta and theta EEG with both frequencies higher in frontal (F3) vs occipital regions (O1) (all p < 0.001). There were no interaction effects and no correlations between qEEG outcomes and morning subjective sleepiness. Reboxetine with and without oxybutynin did not increase neurophysiological markers of next-day morning sleepiness as measured by wake delta and theta EEG power. These findings support the potential safety profile of these agents in respect to next-day sleepiness in people with OSA.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings. ACAM-J produced widespread posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all eight states, and convergent increases in entropy-based complexity over the posterior cortex, with power effects strengthening with phenomenological depth. Crucially, neural complexity remained elevated even in the late, most minimal and unified states, in opposition to the prevailing account that links higher neural entropy to richer phenomenal content. Between practitioners, lower power and higher entropy accompanied more visual and auditory but less bodily content, a redistribution rather than an enrichment of experience; within practitioners, only reduced low-frequency power tracked wider attention and less narrative thought. ACAM-J thus emerges as a non-pharmacological model state at the high-complexity end of the spectrum of altered consciousness, and reveals a previously unquantified dissociation between neural complexity and experiential richness for specific ACAM-J states.

papers.title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for sleep disorders in psychiatry.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are prevalent among psychiatric patients and are strongly associated with neurobiological, psychological, and behavioral processes. This chapter analyzes neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE), an approach incorporating the insights gained from neuroscience with patient education to understand and manage sleep disturbances better. To establish a scientific basis for psychoeducational interventions, we discuss central mechanisms of sleep regulation such as circadian rhythms, sleep homeostasis, neurotransmitter systems, and brain networks. It illustrates how bidirectional sleep disorders and psychiatric syndromes, including depression, anxiety, PTSD, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), are linked, and explains sleep disturbance as a transdiagnostic key clinical feature. In addition to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, NIPE is used to provide a solution to insomnia by integrating mindfulness-based strategies and personalized interventions with the assistance of digital technologies. Implementation challenges and outcome assessment, as well as ethical dimensions of practice, are also considered. In fact, NIPE is a clinically relevant strategy that can both maximize patient engagement and ameliorate sleep disorder outcomes.

papers.title: Trajectories of Sleep and Pain From the Perioperative Period to One-Year After Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality and pain are closely related, and surgery is known to impair sleep quality temporarily. Yet the effects of daily fluctuations in sleep and pain and their impact on long-term outcomes remain insufficiently explored. This prospective cohort study explored bidirectional day-to-day associations between sleep and pain and preoperative predictors of one-year pain outcomes. A total of 171 patients with osteoarthritis scheduled for knee arthroplasty were enrolled. Preoperative assessments included sleep quality, symptoms of anxiety and depression, lifestyle evaluation, and pain intensity. For the first week after surgery, patients reported daily sleep quality and pain intensity. After 1 year, knee pain intensity was reassessed. One hundred and twenty-five patients completed preoperative assessments, 89 completed all seven postoperative daily assessments, and 112 responded after 1 year. Pain peaked on postoperative day two and was significantly lower than preoperative levels at 1 year (p < 0.05). Daily fluctuations in pain and sleep were bidirectionally correlated: higher pain intensity predicted poorer sleep quality the following night (p < 0.05), while poor sleep quality predicted higher next-day pain intensities (p < 0.05). Patients in the worst quartiles of pain and sleep during the first postoperative week reported significantly higher one-year postoperative pain compared to those in the best quartiles (p < 0.05). Preoperative positive affect, with non-significant contributions from sleep quality and symptoms of anxiety, predicted 13.1% (adjusted R2 10.2%) of the variance in one-year postoperative pain. In conclusion, sleep, pain, and psychological factors in the perioperative period are relevant for long-term pain outcomes after knee arthroplasty.

papers.title: Longitudinal resting-state EEG-based modeling predicts phenoconversion and delineates heterogeneity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder is a high-risk prodromal syndrome for Lewy body diseases but highly heterogeneous. Neurophysiologic markers resolving this heterogeneity and predicting phenoconversion remain limited. We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) modeling to longitudinal resting-state EEG from a prospective cohort of 285 participants. SuStaIn identified a progressive degenerative subtype (Subtype 2), characterized by delta/theta increases and lower MoCA scores, and a posterior beta-low subtype (Subtype 1), which was longitudinally unstable and of uncertain independent prognostic significance. Longitudinal validation demonstrated substantial subtype shifting in Subtype 1 and stage advancement predominantly in Subtype 2. In Kaplan-Meier analysis, subtype shifting and accelerated annual stage advancement (ΔStage≥2) identified individuals at exceptionally high phenoconversion risk with survival approaching 0-15% by 7.5 years. These findings extend SuStaIn beyond cross-sectional inference by incorporating longitudinal subtype-shifting and stage-advancement features to stratify prodromal heterogeneity and predict neurodegenerative progression.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) capture neural dynamics across complementary temporal and spatial scales, but analyzing them jointly is difficult: the two modalities differ in measurement mechanisms, temporal resolution, and neurovascular coupling. EEG-fMRI fusion can be framed as an inverse problem, where the goal is to recover latent neural processes only partially observed through electrophysiological and hemodynamic signals. Here, we review data-driven fusion methods published between 2000 and 2025, focusing on techniques that identify shared neural representations across modalities. We organize methods by fusion strategies (symmetric vs. asymmetric), methodological objectives (factorization vs. translation), and modeling assumptions (linear vs. nonlinear), and discuss evaluation metrics and visualization strategies in current use. A recurring finding is the absence of a universal validation standard and the difficulty of interpreting latent multimodal components. Across neurological, psychiatric, and cognitive applications, EEG-fMRI fusion has revealed distributed network dynamics not accessible through unimodal analyses, though temporal misalignment, noise-induced coupling, and model-dependent interpretation remain persistent challenges. We close by discussing directions including nonlinear modeling, flexible coupling frameworks, and large-scale group-level fusion, and situate the field within a broader view of EEG-fMRI fusion as a problem of latent neural inference.

papers.title: Circadian Gating of Neuroimmune Memory: A Shared Persistence-and-Gating Hypothesis for Chronic Pain, Depression, and Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain, depression, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction provide distinct settings in which inflammatory responses and persistent vulnerability may intersect. Evidence for specific cytokine, synaptic, and microglial mechanisms differs across these conditions and does not establish a single comorbidity mechanism. We examine whether circadian context influences the formation or later expression of neuroimmune memory. Circadian regulation of inflammatory responses and innate immune memory each have experimental support, while their coupling in disease-relevant microglia remains unresolved. Human BCG vaccination studies provide a peripheral timing-and-training precedent, which cannot be assumed to operate in the brain. We distinguish immune memory from ongoing inflammation, neuronal chromatin regulation, and sustained symptoms, and separate cell-autonomous microglial timing from rhythmic environmental inputs. The framework generates distinct tests of imprint formation, maintenance, recall, and reversal. A convincing test requires a resolved first challenge, control of initial inflammatory exposure and recall phase, and cell-resolved molecular measurements coupled to altered secondary-response function. Failure to reverse an established imprint would not exclude a role for timing during its formation. Perioperative studies offer a defined exposure but must distinguish delirium from longer-term cognitive decline. This evidence-calibrated hypothesis specifies what must be demonstrated before circadian interventions can be linked to prevention or modification of neuroimmune memory.

papers.title: Beyond the RMMA Index: Respiratory-Event Context and Episode Duration in Adults With Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Sleep Bruxism.
papers.abstract: Sleep bruxism (SB) frequently coexists with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). However, whether rhythmic masticatory muscle activity (RMMA) reflects respiratory recovery, an airway response, or an independent motor phenomenon remains unclear. To characterize the respiratory-event context and duration of RMMA in adults with OSA and SB. Polysomnographic data from 94 adults with OSA and SB were retrospectively analysed. Each RMMA episode was matched to the nearest respiratory event and classified within a 20 s window as pre-respiratory, respiratory-overlap, or post-respiratory; episodes beyond 20 s were considered temporally unrelated. A circular-shift null model assessed whether RMMA-respiratory proximity exceeded within-night chance expectations. Bayesian multinomial mixed-effects models compared RMMA temporal contexts across respiratory-event types, and mixed-effects models assessed arousal linkage and RMMA duration across temporal contexts. Exploratory analyses examined associations between RMMA expression measures and polysomnographic variables. Among 3774 RMMA episodes, 2686 (71.2%) were temporally related to respiratory events, exceeding chance expectations (0.733 vs. 0.273; p < 0.001). Compared with obstructive apnea-related RMMA, central apnea-related RMMA showed higher odds of being pre-respiratory (OR 2.67, 95% CrI 1.76-4.19) and respiratory-overlap (OR 3.26, 95% CrI 2.03-5.29). Of post-respiratory RMMA episodes, 486 (43.0%) occurred within 5 s of respiratory-related arousal onset. Shorter RMMA episode duration was associated with greater respiratory, oxygen desaturation and arousal burden. In this predominantly male, relatively young OSA-SB cohort, RMMA showed heterogeneous temporal organization and RMMA episode duration showed exploratory associations with OSA-related physiological burden.

papers.title: When impulsivity goes wrong: Circadian timing distinguishes which night shift workers succeed and fail.
papers.abstract: Night-shift workers are at increased risk for accidents and injuries, and extant research has focused predominantly on the effect of sleep loss on low-level cognition as a mechanism. Much less is known about the effects of underlying circadian phase on performance, especially as it relates to accident risk. We assessed whether phase angle between circadian timing (dim-light melatonin onset) and task time predicted impulsivity (i.e. action bias, performance, and strategy) in night shift workers. To do this, we used the Stop Light Task, which simulates the complex, and real-world process drivers go through at a stop light (i.e. whether to stop safely or risk going at a yellow light). Thirty night‑shift workers completed the Stop Light Task approximately 13 h after an 8-h in-lab sleep opportunity, and underwent 24 h of hourly saliva collection to assess dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO). Results showed more time between DLMO and task completion (i.e. greater phase angle) was associated with worse performance (i.e. more crashes) and worse overall strategy in the context of risk. Phase angle did not predict action bias (i.e. propensity to run the yellow light), but post-hoc analyses showed greater sleepiness predicted reduced action bias. These results are the first to show circadian processes directly affect impulsivity in night shift workers and determine when someone is likely to be successful or fail in risky situations.

papers.title: Insufficient Sleep, Circadian Targets, Weight Management, and Cardiometabolic Health.
papers.abstract: Insufficient sleep is a potentially modifiable contributor to obesity and cardiometabolic risk, yet sustained sleep extension may be difficult for individuals facing occupational, caregiving, and social constraints. We review emerging literature informing potential timing- and circadian-based strategies that could mitigate obesity risk, even without necessitating an increase in sleep duration. Emerging evidence suggests that the timing of light exposure, food intake, sleep-wake regularity, and physical activity can influence circadian physiology and metabolic health. Insufficient sleep may disrupt these temporal patterns, providing plausible pathways linking insufficient sleep with positive energy balance, weight gain, and metabolic dysfunction. However, few fully powered randomized trials have directly tested the efficacy of interventions targeting these timing-based pathways to mitigate risk of obesity in adults with habitual insufficient sleep. Optimizing the temporal organization of daily behaviors represents a promising complementary approach to obesity prevention and management, especially when increasing sleep duration may not be feasible. However, rigorous trials assessing target engagement, changes in sleep-related outcomes, and clinically meaningful metabolic outcomes are needed.

papers.title: Obesity is associated with alterations in the composition and function of the gut microbiota in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common disorder marked by upper airway collapse, intermittent hypoxia, and sleep disruption. Growing evidence links gut microbiota dysbiosis to OSA-related complications, with obesity as a key risk factor. This study investigates the associations of OSA and obesity status with gut microbiota characteristics. Fecal samples were collected from 65 OSA patients and 15 healthy controls (HCs) and analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Clinical parameters, including body mass index (BMI), apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), lowest oxygen saturation (LSaO2), mean oxygen saturation (MSaO₂), and cumulative time with oxygen saturation below 90% (CT90), were also collected. Linear discriminant analysis effect size (LEfSe) analysis, random forest, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were employed to identify key microbial genera associated with OSA and obesity. Within the OSA cohort, subjects were stratified by BMI into obese OSA (Ob + OSA) and non-obese OSA (Non + OSA) groups to evaluate the association between obesity and the gut microbiota of OSA patients. The gut microbiota of OSA patients exhibited significant differences from that of healthy controls in terms of both community diversity and composition. LEfSe analysis, along with random forest and LASSO regression analyses, revealed a significant enrichment of Blautia, Fusobacterium, and the Eubacterium hallii group in OSA patients, while the abundance of Faecalibacterium was significantly reduced. Functional prediction analysis further indicated significantly enhanced activity in lipid metabolism and digestive system functions in OSA patients compared with healthy controls. Obese OSA (Ob + OSA) patients displayed differences in alpha diversity and the relative abundance of specific microbial taxa compared to non-obese OSA (Non + OSA) patients. The abundance of Synergistota was significantly higher in the Ob + OSA group than in the Non + OSA group, whereas the abundance of Blautia and Bifidobacterium was significantly lower. LEfSe analysis and LASSO regression identified increased Acidaminococcus, Megasphaera, and Morganella and decreased Anaerostipes and Lachnospiraceae UCG-004 as key characteristic genera distinguishing Ob + OSA from Non + OSA. Furthermore, obese patients exhibited more active functional pathways related to the metabolism of terpenoids and polyketides. The gut microbiota of OSA patients markedly differs from that of healthy controls, with obesity being associated with differences in microbial composition. Genera such as Blautia, the Eubacterium hallii group, and Faecalibacterium may serve as potential biomarkers for OSA, while Acidaminococcus, Megasphaera, Morganella, Anaerostipes, and Lachnospiraceae UCG-004 are characteristic of obese OSA patients. These microbial alterations may contribute to OSA pathogenesis and progression. This study provides further insight into gut microbial heterogeneity among OSA patients with different obesity statuses and provides a basis for future prospective and mechanistic studies. This study investigated gut microbiota characteristics in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) according to their obesity status and compared these findings with those in healthy controls. By comparing obese and non-obese patients within the OSA cohort, we identified differences in microbial diversity and the relative abundance of specific taxa associated with obesity status. These findings provide further evidence of heterogeneity in the gut microbiota among OSA patients with different obesity statuses and may help inform future studies investigating the relationships among obesity, OSA, and the gut microbiota.

papers.title: Regular physical activity and a 12-week structured exercise program: Associations with circadian organization and sleep in permanent night-shift workers.
papers.abstract: Permanent night-shift work induces circadian misalignment, sleep disruption, and impaired physiological organization. Although exercise is increasingly recognized as a non-photic zeitgeber, its long-term association with circadian adaptation under occupational conditions remains poorly understood. To examine whether habitual physical activity and a 12-week supervised exercise program are associated with circadian organization, sleep, and physiological rhythms in permanent night-shift workers. Study 1 was a cross-sectional comparison of 12 habitually physically active and 12 sedentary permanent night-shift workers matched for major demographic and occupational characteristics. Study 2 was an uncontrolled longitudinal before-after intervention in 16 initially sedentary workers. Using the same ambulatory protocol, activity-rest rhythms, oral temperature, sleep, and neuromuscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, and cognitive variables were repeatedly assessed across an entire work-rest cycle. Habitually physically active workers exhibited greater rhythm amplitude, dominant oscillatory periods closer to 24 h during the workweek, higher sleep efficiency, and more coherent temporal organization across several physiological systems than sedentary workers. Similar pre-to-post changes were observed in Study 2. During weekend recovery, dominant oscillatory periods transiently shortened to approximately 18-22 h, concurrently with rapid repositioning of activity-rest and oral-temperature acrophases toward diurnal timing. These dynamics most likely reflect adaptive circadian reorganization rather than changes in endogenous circadian period. Regular physical activity was associated with greater circadian robustness, temporal coherence, and better sleep. Because Study 2 lacked a control group, the longitudinal changes cannot be attributed exclusively to the exercise program. Controlled studies using direct phase markers are required.

papers.title: Sleep and Neurodegenerative Diseases: Understanding the Bidirectional Relationship.
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances are pervasive across the spectrum of Lewy body disorders (LBDs), including Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Accumulating clinical, epidemiologic, and neurobiological evidence supports a bidirectional relationship between sleep dysfunction and neurodegeneration, in which pathologic processes disrupt sleep-wake regulation, and impaired sleep may exacerbate neurodegenerative mechanisms, including impaired proteostasis, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and failure of glymphatic clearance. In this review article, the authors synthesize evidence linking sleep and circadian disturbances with LBDs across prodromal, early, and advanced disease stages.

ai.summary: This review synthesizes clinical, epidemiologic, and neurobiological evidence for a bidirectional relationship between sleep/circadian disturbances and Lewy body disorders, including Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, across prodromal, early, and advanced stages. It highlights proposed mechanisms by which sleep dysfunction may exacerbate neurodegeneration, including impaired proteostasis, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and glymphatic clearance failure.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm Disruptions: Causes, Consequences, and Treatment Approaches.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms are intrinsic biological cycles of approximately 24 h that regulate sleep, metabolism, hormone secretion, cardiovascular function, and other physiologic processes. Coordinated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus and molecular clock genes such as CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, and CRY, these rhythms are influenced by external cues, especially light, meal timing, exercise, and social interactions. Circadian disruption contributes to sleep-wake disorders, metabolic dysfunction, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, psychiatric illness, and cancer risk. Assessment tools include melatonin measurements, questionnaires, sleep diaries, and actigraphy. Treatment focuses on optimizing zeitgebers, particularly light exposure and melatonin, to restore circadian alignment and improve health outcomes.

ai.summary: This review describes circadian rhythms coordinated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus and molecular clock genes (CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, CRY), their modulation by zeitgebers such as light, meal timing, and exercise, and the links between circadian disruption and sleep-wake, metabolic, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, psychiatric, and cancer outcomes. It summarizes assessment approaches (melatonin, questionnaires, sleep diaries, actigraphy) and treatments centered on optimizing light exposure and melatonin to restore circadian alignment.

papers.title: A changing educational gradient in age-related sleep duration trajectories across birth cohorts.
papers.abstract: Sleep duration is shaped by both aging and historical context, yet little is known about how age-related sleep trajectories vary across birth cohorts and how these patterns differ by educational attainment and sex. Drawing on a life-course perspective, I examine age and cohort variation in sleep duration and assesses how the educational gradient in sleep duration - that is, differences in sleep duration across educational groups - has changed across generations. Data come from six waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS, 2010-2022). The analytic sample includes 44,379 adults contributing 134,142 person-wave observations. Hierarchical linear models were used to estimate age and cohort trajectories in sleep duration and to examine educational and sex differences in these patterns. Sleep duration declined with age across adulthood and was lower among later-born cohorts than among earlier-born cohorts at comparable ages. Educational attainment further differentiated these age and cohort patterns. Among earlier-born cohorts, adults with higher levels of education reported shorter sleep duration than their less educated peers. This gradient progressively narrowed across successive cohorts, with the relative ordering of educational groups changing at younger cohort-age combinations. Although the cohort pattern was broadly similar among women and men, formal interaction tests indicated sex differences in the age- and cohort-related educational gradients. Additional analyses showed that the changing educational gradient was not materially altered after accounting for observed family, employment, economic, work-time, and health characteristics. Overall, these findings show that educational inequalities in sleep duration are historically contingent, highlighting the importance of linking life-course processes to social change in understanding how the meaning of socioeconomic position and health inequalities evolves across generations.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support. To assess the long-term efficacy and safety of PLWNT in sleep-onset chronic insomnia and to investigate, via multimodal techniques, its modulatory effects on cerebral cortical networks. This prospective, single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3-diagnosed sleep-onset chronic insomnia, randomized 1:1 to a 12-week PLWNT or CBT-I intervention in a superiority design. The primary endpoint is the baseline-to-week-12 change in PSQI total score. Secondary measures include validated scales (ISI, PSAS, HADS, PSS, HAS, MEQ, MFI-20, GSRS, SF-36), sleep diary, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI. Exploratory mechanistic endpoints include (1) EEG-derived spectral power and wPLI within the DMN, SN, and CEN during wakefulness, sleep-onset latency, and sleep stages (N1-N3, REM), and (2) resting-state fMRI connectivity of the same networks. Clinical assessments occur at baseline (week 0), week 6, week 12 (end of intervention), and weeks 16, 20, 24, and 36 after randomization (7 time points); laboratory and imaging measures are obtained at baseline and week 12 only. Primary analysis will use generalized estimating equations on LOCF-imputed data, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. This randomized controlled trial directly compares PLWNT with CBT-I for sleep-onset chronic insomnia, integrating clinical outcome measures with neuroimaging-based mechanistic insights. The findings could position PLWNT as a non-drug therapeutic option backed by objective imaging data.

papers.title: From sleep complaints to clinical phenotypes: A tiered assessment and integrated management framework for sleep comorbidities in Epilepsy-A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are among the most common but frequently underestimated comorbidities in patients with epilepsy, with major manifestations including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, excessive daytime sleepiness, restless legs syndrome, and periodic limb movements of sleep. A complex bidirectional interaction exists between epilepsy and sleep disorders: sleep deprivation, disrupted sleep architecture, and sleep-disordered breathing may increase seizure susceptibility, whereas nocturnal seizures, interictal epileptiform discharges, antiseizure medications, and mood comorbidities may further impair sleep continuity and daytime alertness. Although mechanistic links and individual sleep disorders have received increasing attention, a practical outpatient pathway that connects sleep-related complaints with screening, phenotype recognition, objective testing, and subsequent intervention remains insufficiently defined. From a clinical phenotyping perspective, this review proposes a complaint-based framework for the identification, tiered assessment, and integrated management of sleep comorbidities in epilepsy. The framework translates common sleep complaints into major actionable phenotypes, including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movements of sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, and overlap phenotypes, while incorporating life-course and syndrome-specific considerations for children and adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults, patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, and older adults with epilepsy. This review organizes dispersed evidence on sleep and epilepsy into a clinically oriented conceptual framework linking complaint-based entry, tiered assessment, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment. The framework is intended to facilitate recognition and structured clinical reasoning, while its feasibility and effects on patient outcomes require prospective evaluation.

The framework links sleep complaints to phenotype recognition, objective testing, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment, but its feasibility and outcome effects remain to be prospectively evaluated.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.abstract: Perceptual decisions, a hallmark of cognitive development, become faster and more accurate from early childhood to adulthood, but whether the underlying components mature together, as a single global gain in processing speed would predict, or on separate timetables remains unclear. Behaviour alone cannot distinguish whether age-related improvement reflects clearer sensory encoding, more efficient evidence accumulation, fewer attention lapses or shorter non-decision processes, and prior direct measurements have typically come from small samples spanning limited age ranges. We analysed electroencephalography from 1,534 participants aged 5 to 21 years in the Healthy Brain Network during a contrast-change discrimination task. On the same trials, we measured the visual response and an evidence-accumulation signal, while a decision model estimated accumulation efficiency, attention lapses and non-decision time. We found that the visual response did not grow with age and retained 77% of its strength on missed targets. Instead, accuracy improved through fewer lapses and more efficient accumulation, both reaching half of their developmental change by about 9 years, whereas speed improved later: non-decision time shortened between 11 and 14 years and was longer in children whose accumulation signal rose later. These findings show that perceptual decision-making matures through dissociable stages rather than a single global increase in processing speed: mechanisms supporting accuracy mature in middle childhood, whereas those supporting the fastest responses continue to develop into early adolescence. This framework links developmental theories of processing speed to neural mechanisms of decision-making and provides a reference for identifying which component is disrupted in children who struggle.

papers.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football.
papers.abstract: Late European away fixtures can disrupt sleep, but the influence of immediate return versus overnight stay, and whether responses differ by match participation, remains unclear. Postmatch travel strategy would influence sleep quality and duration across the prematch, match, and subsequent nights, with responses moderated by match participation. Observational repeated-measures field study. Level 3. A total of 19 outfield English Premier League players were monitored across 10 European away fixtures (5 immediate return and 5 overnight stay). Self-reported sleep quality (1 to 7) and sleep duration were recorded on the prematch, match, and subsequent nights. Fixed-effects models examined condition, time, and match participation, with standard errors clustered by player. Sleep quality was lower than prematch baseline on the match and subsequent nights (both β = -0.62 arbitrary units [AU]; P < 0.01; g = -0.63). After overnight stay, sleep quality improved from the match to the subsequent night in players who participated and those who did not (β = 0.69 and 0.63 AU; 95% CIs, 0.37-0.90 and 0.47-0.91; P < 0.01), whereas no change occurred after immediate return. Across participation groups, sleep duration was lower after overnight stay than immediate return on the match night (β = -1.94 hours; P < 0.01; g = -1.26) and subsequent night (β = -1.02 hours; P = 0.02; g = -0.67). However, after overnight stay, sleep duration increased between these nights by 1.45 hours in participants and 1.43 hours in nonparticipants (P < 0.01), with no significant change after immediate return. Participation moderated sleep duration on both postfixture nights (β = 1.27 and 1.64 hours; P ≤ 0.04; g = 0.82 and 1.07). Neither travel strategy was uniformly superior. Overnight stay was associated with poorer absolute sleep duration but a clearer next-night rebound in sleep quality and duration. Postmatch travel should be planned case by case, considering itinerary, next-day demands, and individual match exposure rather than applying a single team-wide policy.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials. To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use. We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression. Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence. Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Circadian Dysregulation in the Choroid Plexus of a Nitroglycerin Rat Model of Chronic Migraine: An RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Migraine patients show choroid plexus (CP) changes, impairing the blood-CSF barrier. The CP regulates circadian rhythms, but links between CP circadian genes and migraine are unexplored. This study examined changes in the CP circadian gene transcriptome in a chronic migraine rat model compared with controls to identify migraine-related pathways. Chronic migraine model: Sprague-Dawley rats (3 females, 3 males) received nitroglycerin (NTG) every other day for 9 days; controls (3 females, 3 males) got saline. CP from the 4th ventricle was collected 2 hours after the final injection for RNA-seq. Migraine Behavior: Von Frey hair tests on days 1, 5, and 9, pre- and 2 hours post-NTG/saline injection, assessed basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds. RNA-seq & Analysis: Differentially expressed genes (p < 0.05, fold change > 1) were identified. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed to assess changes in circadian gene expression. The NTG group showed reduced basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds on days 1, 5, and 9. Females had a greater number of upregulated genes (MT2A, SLC7A11); males had upregulated ZBTB16 and S100A8. SLC7A11, SCG2, and GRIA1 showed inverse regulation (up in females, down in males). Circadian gene expression altered: 10 genes upregulated (e.g., SERPINE1, MAPK9, ATF4), 13 downregulated (e.g., PER2, DBP, EZH2). Sex-specific differences: females (FBXL12, GPR157), males (NKX2-1, ATF4, CLOCK). GO/KEGG analyses revealed significant enrichment of circadian rhythm-related pathways, insulin resistance, and inflammatory response processes, with sex-specific differences: females showed enrichment in HIF-1 signaling and hemoglobin-related pathways, while males exhibited enrichment in arachidonic acid and leukotriene production. CP transcriptomics in the rat migraine model revealed sex-specific gene regulation, with females upregulating antioxidant genes (MT2A, SLC7A11) and males upregulating inflammatory factors (ZBTB16, S100A8), alongside circadian disruption (e.g., SERPINE1 upregulated, PER2 downregulated). Pathway analyses indicate enriched circadian rhythms, HIF-1 signaling (females), inflammatory processes (males), lipid metabolism (PPARα), and heme signaling, highlighting sex-specific and circadian targets for migraine therapy.

papers.title: SIRT7 Aggravates Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Neuronal Apoptosis via Decreasing Succinylation and Cascaded Ubiquitylation of NFL.
papers.abstract: Insomnia affected one-third of the global population, but its molecular mechanism was not clarified. A chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) model was constructed in SD rats using multiple platforms over water. Hippocampal tissues were collected for ubiquitinomics and succinylomics. Sirtuin 7 (SIRT7) inhibitor was administered to elevate succinylation levels. Molecular experiments demonstrated the cascade reaction of succinylation and ubiquitylation, and Neurofilament Light (NFL)-binding ubiquitinating enzyme. Chronic sleep deprivation caused cognitive disorder of rats. Mostly, succinylation and ubiquitylation displayed a downregulated trend in the CSD group, especially double modification of NFL at K370 (succinylation site) and K267/281 (ubiquitylation site), whose protein level was upregulated in CSD rats. NFL was proved to be a target of SIRT7, a well-known desuccinylase. SIRT7 inhibitor weakened cognitive deficit, blocked neuronal apoptosis, decreased NFL expression, and increased succinylation and ubiquitylation levels, which were inverse in the CSD model and cells infected with SIRT7 overexpression adenovirus. SIRT7 suppressed not only succinylation but also ubiquitylation through K370 of NFL. Knockdown of NFL receded cognitive disorder and neuronal apoptosis. BRCA1 Associated Deubiquitinase 1 (BAP1) inhibited NFL ubiquitylation and subsequently degradation. SIRT7 inhibitor promoted succinylation and cascaded ubiquitylation, as well as disrupting the interaction between BAP1 and NFL, finally suppressing CSD.

SIRT7 inhibition or NFL knockdown attenuated these deficits, implicating SIRT7-NFL succinylation/ubiquitylation in insomnia-related cognitive decline.

papers.title: Extreme delta brush as an ictal pattern in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
papers.abstract: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis frequently presents with psychiatric symptoms, seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and characteristic electroencephalographic (EEG) abnormalities including extreme delta brush (EDB). Differentiating epileptic from non-epileptic dyskinetic movements remains challenging, and the ictal versus interictal nature of EDB remains incompletely understood. In this case, a 22-year-old man developed neuropsychiatric symptoms progressing to hallucinations, confusion, abnormal speech, dyskinetic movements, and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Brain MRI was unremarkable. Cerebrospinal fluid demonstrated positive anti-NMDAR antibodies. Continuous EEG initially showed diffuse slowing without correlation to dyskinetic movements of grimacing, jaw thrusting, and limb posturing. During treatment, abundant stereotyped episodes of facial pulling with rhythmic lip twitching emerged and were found on EEG to have an ictal correlate consistent with focal motor status epilepticus. Following reduction in ictal burden, EEG demonstrated a striking pattern of highly stereotyped right jaw movement and right arm internal rotation synchronized to complexes of midline beta-gamma activity overriding each delta wave peak, qualifying as a definite EDB pattern with clinical correlate to each EDB complex. Thus, in this case, EDB was an ictal pattern. This case illustrates the overlap between seizures and dyskinesias in anti-NMDAR encephalitis and highlights characteristic EEG findings including the EDB pattern. Unlike classic descriptions of EDB as a non-ictal EEG biomarker of severe anti-NMDAR encephalitis, this patient demonstrated clinical motor events time-locked to each EDB complex, supporting the possibility that EDB patterns represent ictal phenomena, at least in some cases such as this one. Continuous EEG monitoring is essential to distinguish electroclinical seizures from dyskinesias and may provide further insight into the potentially ictal significance of EDB.

The case highlights overlap between seizures and dyskinesias and the value of continuous EEG for distinguishing electroclinical seizures from dyskinetic movements.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Exacerbates Pulpal Inflammation and Impairs Repair Through Dysregulated Neutrophil Activity in Rats.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of sleep deprivation on pulpal inflammation and repair and determine the contribution of neutrophil activity to these changes in rat models. Sleep deprivation was induced in rats using a modified multiple platform method. Pulp responses were evaluated using three experimental settings. Under baseline conditions, rats underwent acute sleep deprivation for four consecutive days. In the inflammatory model, pulpitis was induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and assessed 1-4 days after induction. In the reparative model, direct pulp capping (DPC) was performed and pulpal healing was assessed at 14 and 28 days during sleep deprivation. Histological, vascular and inflammatory changes were evaluated by haematoxylin and eosin staining, Masson's trichrome staining, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence. Transcriptomic alterations in pulp tissue were analysed by mRNA sequencing. Neutrophil abundance and activation were assessed in peripheral blood and dental pulp by complete blood counts, flow cytometry and myeloperoxidase staining. To investigate the functional contribution of neutrophils and neutrophil elastase (NE), sleep-deprived rats were treated with the neutrophil-depleting antibody or the NE inhibitor Sivelestat. Sleep deprivation disrupted pulpal homeostasis, inducing vascular alterations and inflammatory cell infiltration. Following DPC, sleep-deprived rats exhibited impaired repair, including incomplete hard tissue bridge formation and reduced osteopontin expression at Day 14, followed by pulpal necrosis and apical periodontitis at Day 28. In the LPS-induced pulpitis model, sleep deprivation accelerated inflammatory progression and increased pulpal necrosis and leukocyte accumulation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of immune- and neutrophil-associated pathways. Sleep deprivation increased neutrophil abundance, accumulation and activation in dental pulp, accompanied by elevated NE expression and enhanced neutrophil extracellular trap-like signals. Neutrophil depletion attenuated pulpal inflammation and tissue injury, while pharmacological inhibition of NE reduced inflammatory responses and pulpal tissue damage. Sleep deprivation exacerbates pulpal inflammation and impairs repair, at least in part through enhanced neutrophil activity and NE-mediated tissue injury. These findings reveal a mechanistic link between sleep disturbance and dysregulated pulpal inflammation and suggest neutrophil/NE-associated pathways as potential targets for further investigation.

papers.title: A 6-week vegan Mediterranean diet reduces neutrophil count and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio compared with a traditional Mediterranean diet in women with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) is associated with a low-grade pro-inflammatory profile, reflected by elevated neutrophil counts and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), that may impair function. Evidence on the effects of a vegan Mediterranean diet on inflammation, functional outcomes, and quality of life remains limited. This secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a 6-week vegan Mediterranean diet vs a traditional Mediterranean diet in women with FM on inflammatory and functional outcomes, with particular focus on NLR and functional performance. We hypothesized that a vegan Mediterranean diet would reduce neutrophil count and NLR more than a traditional Mediterranean diet in women with FM. Twenty-five women with FM were initially randomly assigned to either the traditional Mediterranean group (n = 12) or the vegan Mediterranean group (n = 13). Both diets were isocaloric and matched for macronutrient distribution. The outcomes evaluated included the NLR, white blood cell count, functional performance (Five-Times-Sit-To-Stand [FTSTS] and Timed Up and Go [TUG], kinesiophobia [Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia], sleep quality [Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index] and fatigue [Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory]). Compared to the traditional Mediterranean diet, the vegan Mediterranean diet significantly reduced NLR (P = .026; ES = 0.23) and neutrophil count (P = .037; ES = 0.21). However, no significant between-group differences were observed for kinesiophobia, sleep quality, fatigue or functional performance. A vegan Mediterranean diet improves systemic inflammatory profile, reflected by reductions in NLR and neutrophil count, in women with FM compared with a traditional Mediterranean diet. Longer-term studies are needed to confirm whether these changes translate into functional improvements.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and variable intellectual and behavioral abnormalities (NEDHIB) is a rare autosomal-dominant condition caused by pathogenic POLR2A variants. It typically presents in infancy with hypotonia, developmental delay, and multisystem manifestations. Fewer than 40 patients have been reported worldwide, suggesting frequent misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. To our knowledge, neurodevelopmental regression has not been documented in confirmed NEDHIB cases, and no standardized therapeutic regimens are established for clinical management. The patient presented with neonatal hypotonia and developmental delay. At 2 years and 4 months, she developed sleep-associated dystonia-like nodding and limb tremors that were initially suspected to represent epileptic seizures. By 3 years of age, she exhibited marked neurodevelopmental regression: loss of the ability to walk and sit independently, together with deterioration of language function. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated background slowing accompanied by epileptiform discharges. Whole-exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous POLR2A variant c.3379C > T (p. L1127F), which confirmed the diagnosis of NEDHIB. Long-term rehabilitation training yielded only modest clinical benefits. After initiation of the dopamine agent levodopa-benserazide hydrochloride, marked improvements in motor and cognitive performance were observed, accompanied by the complete resolution of nodding episodes. With dose titration during follow-up, her clinical status remained stable without symptom relapse. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum associated with POLR2A-related NEDHIB and suggests that neurodevelopmental regression may occur within the phenotypic spectrum of this disorder. Our findings also highlight the potential benefit of low-dose dopamine therapy, offering novel insights into the clinical diagnosis, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic management of NEDHIB.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery electroencephalography often provides limited subject-specific supervision. This study tested whether complementary leaky integrate-and-fire (CLIF)-family temporal-state decoding shows a decoder-level advantage after the EEG representation is fixed, how that advantage changes with decoder-label availability, and whether hard binary spikes are required. ANN-SEW, the artificial neural network comparator with spike-element-wise (SEW) residual topology, and SEW-CLIF received identical frozen attention-based temporal convolutional network (ATCNet) and filter-bank convolutional network (FBCNet) representations. The evidence chain combined BCI Competition IV Dataset 2a (BCI2a) development, retrospective OpenBMI replication, an internally pre-access-held-out BCI Competition IV Dataset 2b (BCI2b) evaluation, cross-entropy-only label-budget analyses, and a separate internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 Session-A-to-Session-B evaluation. Additional robustness analyses included shared whole-sequence readout for parameter-matched gated recurrent unit (GRU) and temporal convolutional network (TCN) decoders, exact-gradient sigmoid-gated Soft-CLIF, equal optimizer-update budgets, a within-BCI2a binary sensitivity analysis, and computational profiling. Under cross-entropy-only training, SEW-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 10.082 percentage points (pp) on BCI2a and 5.470 pp. on OpenBMI, while full-budget BCI2b remained near parity (+0.181 pp). The ANN-relative gap decreased as decoder labels increased and persisted under equal-update training. At 25 labels/class, exact-gradient Soft-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 11.085, 8.479, and 5.809 pp. on BCI2a, BCI2b, and OpenBMI, respectively. With matched whole-sequence readout, hard SEW-CLIF was broadly comparable to GRU-Stat and TCN-Stat on BCI2a and BCI2b and modestly higher on OpenBMI. The internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 evaluation showed the same attenuation, with a slope of -2.319 pp. per label doubling (95% CI, -4.118 to -0.604). CLIF-family temporal-state dynamics show a reproducible decoder-label-regime effect under frozen supervised representations. Hard forward discretization is not required for the ANN-relative effect, and matched temporal readout substantially reduces differences between CLIF and other continuous temporal decoders.

papers.title: The effect of web-based education and therapeutic play methods provided to children undergoing elective surgery on preoperative anxiety and fear, and postoperative pain and sleep: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of combining web-based education provided at home with therapeutic play implemented in the hospital on preoperative anxiety and fear, as well as postoperative pain and sleep, in children aged 7-12 years undergoing elective surgery. Randomized controlled experimental study. The study included 78 children aged 7-12 years who underwent elective surgery. The children were randomly assigned to two groups: intervention (n = 37) and control (n = 41). Children in the intervention group received web-based education about the surgical process at home and information through therapeutic play at the hospital, whereas the control group received standard preoperative nursing care. Data were collected using the Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale-Short Form (mYPAS-SF), Child Fear Scale (CFS), Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale (WBFPS), and Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC). The preoperative mYPAS-SF and CFS scores, as well as the postoperative WBFPS scores, were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (p < 0.05), with effect sizes indicating large clinical significance. No significant difference was found between the groups in terms of post-discharge SDSC scores (p > 0.05), and the effect size was clinically small. Providing preoperative preparation education using a combination of web-based education and therapeutic play was effective in reducing preoperative anxiety and fear and postoperative pain in children undergoing elective surgery; however, it did not affect improving sleep. Pediatric nurses can help reduce children's preoperative anxiety, fear, and postoperative pain in children scheduled for surgery by using effective, practical, web-based educational and therapeutic play methods tailored to the children's age and developmental characteristics in pediatric surgery clinics.

papers.title: Suspected Functional Adrenal Insufficiency and Unmasking of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Case for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Restraint.
papers.abstract: A man in his 30s presented with progressive weight loss, fatigue, anorexia, and low mood that developed over several weeks following international migration and transition to night shift work, the changes that disrupted his sleep-wake cycle and circadian rhythm. A low 8 am cortisol level (2.9 mcg/dL) with a borderline low ACTH concentration (7.4 pg/mL), negative anti-adrenal antibodies, normal electrolytes, and unremarkable adrenal imaging, suggestive of secondary adrenal insufficiency. Given his hemodynamic stability, empirical glucocorticoid therapy was deliberately deferred in favor of cessation of night shift work, sleep restoration, and nutritional rehabilitation, which resulted in complete clinical and biochemical resolution within weeks. At six months follow-up, a rising thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level, strongly positive thyroid peroxidase antibodies, and a heterogeneous thyroid on ultrasound revealed previously unrecognized Hashimoto's thyroiditis, a finding consistent with cortisol inhibitory effect on TSH secretion during adrenal suppression. This case illustrates that circadian rhythm disruption from night shift work and migration can produce a reversible functional form of secondary adrenal insufficiency that may resolve without glucocorticoid replacement. It underscores the value of detailed occupational and sleep history in patients presenting with unexplained constitutional symptoms and highlights how cortisol-TSH interactions can transiently mask the co-existing autoimmune thyroid disease. Clinicians should consider a period of clinical reassessment before treating hemodynamically stable patients with long-term glucocorticoid therapy and should reassess thyroid function once adrenal function normalizes.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a prodromal stage of Parkinson's disease (PD). This study aimed to investigate whether gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) show consistent alterations in iRBD and PD with RBD patients. We enrolled 29 iRBD, 24 PD with RBD, 17 PD without RBD, and 18 normal controls (NC). Fecal microbiota composition was analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing, and SCFA concentrations via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Clinical symptoms were assessed using motor and non-motor scales, and Spearman correlation analysis was performed to explore interrelationships. Microbiota analysis revealed that, compared with NC, Bifidobacterium, Blautia_A, and Azospira_A were significantly enriched, whereas Agathobaculum, Clostridium_Q, Faecalibaculum, Photobacterium, Copromonas, UBA3402, Acetobacter, and Sutterella were reduced in both iRBD and PD with RBD groups. SCFA analysis showed significantly decreased fecal butyric acid and propionic acid levels in both groups versus NC. Correlation analysis demonstrated that in the iRBD group, Bifidobacterium positively correlated with RBD disease duration; butyric acid negatively correlated with NMSS and RBD-HK; propionic acid negatively correlated with NMSS, RBD-HK, and SCOPA-AUT. In the PD with RBD group, Bifidobacterium negatively correlated with SCOPA-AUT and positively with HAMD-17; butyric acid positively correlated with MDS-UPDRS III. iRBD and PD with RBD share similar gut dysbiosis and SCFA abnormalities. Elevated Bifidobacterium and decreased butyric acid and propionic acid are candidate markers for iRBD risk stratification, but correlation does not imply predictive ability. Their value in predicting progression to PD requires validation in longitudinal iRBD cohorts.

papers.title: Circadian orchestration of the cutaneous microenvironment and chronotherapeutic strategies in inflammatory skin diseases.
papers.abstract: The clinical course of inflammatory skin diseases-encompassing atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and chronic spontaneous urticaria-frequently exhibits pronounced symptomatic rhythmicity, most classically manifested as the nocturnal exacerbation of pruritus. Although previous studies have progressively elucidated the circadian mechanisms governing both the epidermal barrier and local immunity that drive lesion evolution, contemporary clinical regimens for most targeted therapeutics and biologics have yet to incorporate administration timing as a key variable for optimizing efficacy. This review systematically delineates the dynamic interactive network between skin barrier function and the immune microenvironment under the regulation of the endogenous circadian clock. Building upon this mechanistic foundation, we examine how the timing of each major drug class-topical agents, conventional systemic drugs, oral small molecules and macromolecular biologics-could be aligned with the circadian peaks of the mediators they target, and we distinguish the components of this framework that are supported by clinical data from those that remain hypotheses. Ultimately, by conceptualizing chronotherapeutic strategies for precise intervention in local microenvironmental rhythms, this article aims to provide a testable framework for future chronotherapeutic research in inflammatory skin diseases.

papers.title: Perioperative methadone: Clinical use and knowledge among Australian anaesthetists.
papers.abstract: Intravenous methadone has re-emerged as a perioperative analgesic, yet uncertainty persists regarding its optimal use. Variation in clinician practice and interpretation of pharmacological principles may influence its safe and effective application. We conducted a mixed-methods survey-based study within a national anaesthesia educational programme (ADVANCE). A voluntary, anonymous pre-presentation clinician survey was distributed to predominantly Australian anaesthetists to characterise methadone use, dosing strategies, adjunct prescribing and patient selection. Real-time audience polling during the educational session assessed clinician responses to pharmacology-based and clinical decision-making scenarios. Survey and polling datasets were analysed independently using descriptive statistics. A total of 726 clinicians completed the survey. Overall, 50.6% (n = 367) of respondents reported using methadone. Among users (n = 367), practice varied widely across surgical contexts and dosing strategies, including weight-based, fixed and procedure-dependent approaches. Concurrent administration of additional opioids and central nervous system depressants was common (86.1%). Clinicians reported avoiding methadone in specific patient groups, most frequently frail patients, those with prolonged QT interval, or obstructive sleep apnoea. Polling responses demonstrated variability in clinician interpretation of pharmacological principles, particularly regarding timing of central effects. Perioperative methadone use is characterised by substantial variation in uptake, dosing and adjunct prescribing. Variability in clinician responses relative to pharmacological reference data, combined with frequent co-administration of additional opioids and sedatives, highlights potential areas for targeted education and institutional safeguards to support safe implementation.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making early prevention a public health priority. Emerging adulthood (18-29 years) is a critical period for establishing lifelong cardiovascular health behaviors, yet adherence to the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) health behaviors remains suboptimal among this population. To synthesize evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, and LE8 health behaviors among emerging adults within the Health Belief Model. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. English-language publications (2000-November 2025) examining hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, or LE8 health behaviors were reviewed. Findings were synthesized using a Health Belief Model-guided narrative approach. Thirty-nine studies were included. Hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge alone appeared insufficient to promote sustained engagement in LE8 health behaviors. Emerging adults frequently underestimated their cardiovascular risk despite modifiable risk factors. Self-efficacy may facilitate the translation of cardiovascular risk awareness and motivation into healthy behaviors. The synthesis informed a proposed HBM-guided framework in which knowledge may inform cardiovascular risk perception, risk perception may strengthen motivation for preventive action, and self-efficacy may facilitate healthy eating, physical activity, nicotine avoidance, and adequate sleep. These proposed relationships require empirical testing. Cardiovascular disease prevention among emerging adults requires more than education. Interventions should strengthen cardiovascular risk perception and self-efficacy while addressing social and structural barriers. The proposed framework provides a theory-informed foundation for cardiovascular nursing practice, future research, and intervention development.

papers.title: Atypical delusional misidentification with alternating impostors in a single body: a case report.
papers.abstract: Delusional misidentification syndromes (DMS), including Capgras and Fregoli syndromes, involve disturbances in identifying familiar individuals. Atypical presentations may challenge traditional classification and illuminate processes underlying familiarity and personal identity. A 42-year-old woman presented with persecutory and grandiose delusions alongside an unusual misidentification belief concerning her husband. Despite his unchanged physical appearance, she believed that different individuals alternately inhabited his body. She expressed complete conviction without insight, while remaining organised, fully oriented, and functionally independent. Neurological examination and routine laboratory and urine investigations were unremarkable. Neuroimaging, EEG, and formal neuropsychological assessment were not performed. Voluntary hospitalisation was offered but declined, and the patient was subsequently lost to follow-up. The presentation shares features with Capgras syndrome, through rejection of a familiar person as genuine, and Fregoli syndrome, through identity instability, but does not fully correspond to either. Unlike classical descriptions involving replacement or disguise, multiple identities were attributed to one physically unchanged familiar person. This may reflect a disturbed continuity of perceived personal identity rather than facial recognition alone. This case illustrates an atypical DMS presentation beyond traditional categorical definitions. Careful phenomenological characterisation of recognition, familiarity, and identity may help clarify atypical misidentification phenomena.
